The Pro League encounter between Al Najma and Al Shabab on May 20, 2026, brought together two sides determined to assert their dominance in a high-stakes league fixture. Fans at the stadium witnessed a clash defined by tactical discipline and physical intensity from the opening whistle. First Half Drama and the Breakthrough The match began with a series of heavy challenges as both teams fought for control of the midfield. This combative atmosphere led to three early bookings within the first 30 minutes, with Rakan Al-Tulayhi , Wesley Hoedt , and Abdulaziz Al Harabi all seeing yellow. Just as the first half seemed destined to end goalless, a pivotal moment arrived in the 45th minute. Al Najma were awarded a penalty, and Lazaro stepped up to calmly slot the ball home, giving the hosts a vital lead. The tension continued into stoppage time, where Mohammed Al Fatil also found his way into the referee's book. Discipline and Tactical Shifts in the Second Half The second period saw both managers turning to their benches to find a solution. Al Shabab introduced Abdullah Saeed immediately after the break, but their rhythm was disrupted by further yellow cards for Nawaf Al-Hawsawi and Haroune Camara . As the clock ticked down, a wave of substitutions followed, including the introduction of Unai Hernandez and Bilal Boutobba , as the visitors searched desperately for an equalizer. In the closing stages, Al Najma focused on game management to preserve their narrow lead. Nasser Al-Haleel and the goal-scorer Lazaro both received late yellow cards as the game grew increasingly fractious. In the 90+6th minute, Lazaro was replaced by Mohammed Mile to shore up the defense for the final seconds. Despite the late pressure, the home side held firm to secure all three points in a match where a single clinical strike from the penalty spot proved to be the difference.

Expectations were high at the stadium as Al Shabab faced off against Al Ittihad FC in a crucial Pro League fixture held on May 17, 2026. Both sides entered the pitch fully aware that every moment would be decisive in their quest for league supremacy. A Second Half Offensive Surge After a cagey first half, the match ignited shortly after the break. Al Shabab broke the deadlock in the 54th minute, with Ali Al-Bulayhi finding the net following an assist from Yannick Carrasco . The momentum swung decisively in favor of the hosts just minutes later when Haroune Camara , set up again by Carrasco , doubled the lead to 2-0. Al Ittihad FC responded with urgency, and Houssem Aouar managed to claw a goal back in the 67th minute, setting the stage for a tense finale. Late Drama and Red Card Chaos As the match entered the dying stages, the intensity reached a boiling point. Yannick Carrasco capped off his dominant display by scoring the third goal for Al Shabab in the 88th minute, assisted by Ali Al-Azaizeh . However, the closing minutes turned chaotic; Abdulaziz Al-Othman was sent off in the 90+1 minute, leaving the hosts to defend their lead with ten men. Al Ittihad FC pushed hard and finally found a second goal through Danilo Pereira in the 90+9 minute, following a cross from Ahmed Al-Julaydan , but the final whistle blew shortly after, securing the result for Al Shabab .

João Félix Ignites the Match The contest began with an explosive tempo that favored the visitors almost immediately. João Félix showcased his clinical finishing by finding the back of the net in just the 3rd minute of play. Before the home side could catch their breath, the Portuguese star struck again in the 10th minute, expertly converting a chance created by Abdulrahman Ghareeb . This early two-goal cushion put Al Nassr in a commanding position, forcing Al Shabab to rethink their defensive strategy under immense pressure. Al Shabab's Resilient Fightback Despite the early setbacks, Al Shabab refused to go down without a fight and gradually clawed their way back into the game. The strike revitalized the home crowd and shifted the momentum, leading to a balanced period of play where both sides traded blows. Late Drama and a Hattrick Seal The second half remained a tightly contested affair until the final fifteen minutes sparked a flurry of action. In the 75th minute, Cristiano Ronaldo extended the lead after being set up by Sadio Mane . However, the drama was far from over; Ali Al-Bulayhi struck back for Al Shabab in the 80th minute following an assist from Hammam Al-Hammami , making it 2-3 and setting up a grandstand finish. The closing stages were high-tempered, resulting in yellow cards for Saad Balobaid and Salem Al Najdi . Deep into stoppage time, the tension reached its peak when Al Nassr was awarded a penalty. The goal secured a 2-4 victory, and although the match continued until the 90+11th minute, the outcome was no longer in doubt as the referee blew the final whistle on a pulsating footballing spectacle.

The Pro League atmosphere was electric on May 11, 2026, as Neom SC hosted Al Shabab in a fixture that promised tactical intrigue and high-intensity football. Fans gathered to witness a battle of wills where every decision on the pitch would carry immense weight for both sides' ambitions. Benrahma's Dead-Eye Accuracy from the Spot The opening exchanges were marked by physical play, with Mohammed Al Shwirekh receiving an early yellow card in the 17th minute. This set the tone for a period of pressure that saw Neom SC take control through set-piece opportunities. Said Benrahma emerged as the central figure of the first half, demonstrating nerves of steel by converting two crucial penalties. The first came in the 19th minute, followed by a second clinical finish from the spot right at the 45-minute mark, giving his side a significant advantage before the interval. Al Shabab's Fightback and Late Drama The second half began with a flurry of tactical changes, as Neom SC opted to replace their goalscorer Benrahma with Muhannad Al Saad , while Ali Al Asmari and Abdulaziz Al-Othman also entered the fray. Al Shabab refused to go down without a fight, steadily building pressure as the clock ticked down. Their persistence paid off in the 78th minute when Yacine Adli orchestrated a brilliant move to find Yannick Carrasco , who finished with precision to breathe new life into the contest. As the match entered its final stages, the tension boiled over, resulting in yellow cards for Khalifah Aldawsari and later Abdulaziz Al-Othman deep in stoppage time. Both managers utilized their benches to manage the closing minutes, with Mohammed Al Burayk and Hawsawi Ahmed coming on to stabilize the defensive lines. Despite Al Shabab's late push for an equalizer, the final whistle blew after seven minutes of added time, confirming a hard-fought result in this Pro League encounter.
